subject: Bantha
social_quote: All banthas were peaceful omnivores and lived in herds.
domestic_quote: They were social herd animals, and were often domesticated
dimorphism_note: Legends image Bantha_Bull_and_Cow.jpg (viewed): bull has larger double-spiral horns and bigger head; cow a single spiral. Text: "bulls were larger than cows" (canon_references/bantha).

subject: Eopie
social_quote: They were very social creatures that lived in large herds of 20 or more.
domestic_quote: were domesticated by the planet's inhabitants

subject: Dewback
social_quote: wild dewbacks were also known to roam the seemingly endless deserts of Tatooine in single-file packs of two to five
domestic_quote: where they were used as beasts of burden, as well as mounts
dimorphism_note: Males display bellies that change to sky-blue when courting (display colouring, not a fixed look).
note: Same Legends sentence opens "While they had a reputation for being solitary animals"; another source (The Wildlife of Star Wars) says herds. Small-group grazer.

subject: Fambaa
social_quote: In the wild, fambaas traveled in herds of up to twelve
domestic_quote: The fambaa had been domesticated by Gungans for millennia as beasts of burden

subject: Falumpaset
social_quote: in large herds (as well as in family groups containing one adult bull and four to seven adult cows and their young)
domestic_quote: Easily domesticated, falumpasets were popular mounts all over the galaxy.
dimorphism_note: Bull/cow named; no stated look difference.

subject: Shaak
social_quote: Shaaks were plump quadrupedal herd animals native to the grasslands of Naboo.
domestic_quote: Gungans farmed shaaks for their meat and hide.

subject: Nerf
social_quote: evolved to tell apart different herds
domestic_quote: Individuals who herded nerfs for a living were referred to as nerf herders.
dimorphism_note: Male nerfs were generally larger and more aggressive than their female counterparts, with more pronounced horns.
note: RSW_FeralNerf is our sub-variety; inherits nerf lore.

subject: Reek
social_quote: Reeks were usually found in herds
domestic_quote: They could also be found on Tatooine and in ranches on the Codian Moon and Saleucami.
dimorphism_note: The horns of male reeks are usually larger than those of females (also canon_references/iridonianreek).

subject: Jakobeast
social_quote: Jakobeasts were Force-sensitive arctic herd animals
domestic_quote: Jakobeasts were domesticated primarily for their meat, milk, and fur.
dimorphism_note: "elder bulls turned outward" - no look difference stated.
note: Canon: "ill-suited to serve as mounts, guards, or attack animals".

subject: Kybuck
social_quote: Pav-ti tracked a small herd of kybucks
domestic_quote: Some chieftains often domesticated kybucks as a symbol of status.
dimorphism_note: Males had short horns sitting atop their head.

subject: Uvak
social_quote: stole an entire herd of uvak from the port town of Eorm
domestic_quote: tamed and domesticated the uvaks

subject: Varactyl
social_quote: had a brief encounter with a herd of varactyls
domestic_quote: incredibly loyal and obedient mounts
dimorphism_note: While females sported blue-green plumage and skin, males were mostly dull shades of orange and brown. (Legends image shows Boga, a female only.)

subject: Gornt
social_quote: Wild gornts traveled in packs of 10 to 30, with half of the pack being young gornts
domestic_quote: The gornt was a domesticated, omnivorous creature
note: Canon word is "packs" but grazing livestock with young; caption "A herd of Gornts".

subject: Zeer
social_quote: Zeer traveled in herds
note: Shown at the Coruscant Livestock Exchange (image caption) and in zoos/circuses; no domestication statement.

subject: Beldon
social_quote: They traveled in free-floating herds numbering anywhere from 500 to 3,000.

subject: Iriaz
social_quote: They lived in massive herds
note: "lone iriaz were usually sick, old, or injured, though the occasional rogue male".

subject: Kwi
social_quote: When traveling in herds across the plains

subject: Hrumph
social_quote: Herds defended young from predators like veermoks by encircling them

subject: Corinathoth
social_quote: encountered a herd of Korinatoths crossing the plains of Maridun

subject: Woolamander
social_quote: babies would become members of troops numbering 20 individuals

subject: Mott
social_quote: Communes usually consisted of a dominant male and, perhaps, one lieutenant male that guarded the females and young.
domestic_quote: Gungans found motts to be good pets
dimorphism_note: Legends image shows female + young only.

subject: Scurrier
social_quote: Scurriers traveled in packs of around thirty
dimorphism_note: Horns: those of a male were thick and curved, while those of a female were thin and straight. (Legends image shows a female only.)
note: Canon word is "packs" but they scatter from danger - a flee-group, not a hunting pack.

subject: Kowakian monkey-lizard
social_quote: rarely leaving the packs they moved around in for protection against predators
domestic_quote: often used by members of the underworld as pets
note: Canon also: "impossible to train a monkey-lizard". Oldest female leads.

subject: Pikobi
social_quote: The Pikobi traveled in pairs or groups of five to six.
note: Group-living; canon does not say they hunt together.

subject: Clodhopper
social_quote: they fed in swarms, becoming a real menace
note: Flightless crop-pest birds.

subject: Jerba
social_quote: a pack of anoobas killed or scattered Corey's entire herd
domestic_quote: The jerba was an equine pack animal and beast of burden
note: Herd evidence is of a kept herd, not wild.

subject: Womp rat
social_quote: Womp rats were not timid creatures, hunting in packs
note: Canon: "not unheard of for people to have domesticated womp rats as pets" - occasional pet, pest otherwise.

subject: Gutkurr
social_quote: Gutkurrs were pack hunters
domestic_quote: for centuries they have been exported by crime lords as pets
note: "intelligent enough to be trained - but only by those brave enough".

subject: Anooba
social_quote: Anoobas were aggressive pack predators native to Tatooine.
domestic_quote: Anoobas could be trained to be pets,guards,or hunters.
dimorphism_note: males being larger than females (20-45 kg range).

subject: Cannok
social_quote: these packs were usually formed of three or more cannoks

subject: Marsh haunt
social_quote: they worked in loose packs of two to eight creatures to ambush prey

subject: Massiff
social_quote: A pack of massiffs on Tatooine
domestic_quote: Massiffs were often domesticated for sentry and guard tasks

subject: Vornskr
social_quote: A pack of vornskrs
domestic_quote: kept two vornskrs, Sturm and Drang, as pets and guard animals
note: Social evidence is an image caption.

subject: Vulptex
social_quote: They lived in groups referred to as skulks, regrouping three to four families with as many as ten creatures by family.

subject: Kreetle
social_quote: They attack in groups of four-to-five

subject: Hawk-bat
social_quote: Flocks of hawk-bats would hunt and attack their prey as if they were one.

subject: Shyrack
social_quote: These winged monstrosities were eyeless beasts that hunted in swarms.
note: Also "fiercely territorial" (as a cave colony).

subject: Sketto
social_quote: Sketto tended to swarm with others of their kind to suck the blood of sleeping larger animals.

subject: Mynock
social_quote: tended to flock together in a pack of ten
note: Also "extremely territorial". Energy parasites, not hunters - "pack" is canon wording.

subject: Lylek
social_quote: These hordes were led by a lylek queen
dimorphism_note: Queen caste exists.
note: Hive insect.

subject: Kinrath
social_quote: a single female kinrath matriarch was the leader of a hive of kinrath
dimorphism_note: Matriarch caste stated.
note: Also "territorial".

subject: Krykna
social_quote: cocooned their prey in underground hives
note: Canon: "extremely difficult to tame with the Force".

subject: Neebray
social_quote: Groups of neebray were called a pod.

subject: Mee
social_quote: Mee were plentiful, traveling in schools of thousands

subject: Faa
social_quote: a school of faa—which could include up to thirty fish
domestic_quote: Faa were sold in pet shops on Coruscant.
note: Pet-shop trade only.

subject: Peko-peko
social_quote: Peko-pekos congregated in large flocks but generally traveled in pairs and mated for life.
domestic_quote: they were a favorite pet of both Gungans and Naboo
dimorphism_note: Both male and female had beautiful indigo-sapphire plumage, and both were the same size.

subject: Porg
social_quote: A group of porgs was called a "murder."
domestic_quote: Both wild and domesticated porgs were unusually smitten by human objects.
dimorphism_note: Porgs were sexually dimorphic; males were slightly larger than females and had orange plumage around the eyes.

subject: Voorpak
social_quote: In the wild, they lived in small colonies
domestic_quote: They came from Naboo and were often kept as pets.

subject: Ronto
social_quote: While typically encountered in small groups
domestic_quote: Easily domesticated, rontos were utilized by the Jawas as beasts of burden
dimorphism_note: Female in heat gives off musky scent (not visual).
note: Legends only for the group statement.

subject: Horax
social_quote: The carnivorous horaxes were solitary creatures.

subject: Zakkeg
social_quote: Huge, armored quadrupeds, they were solitary and territorial.

subject: Wampa
social_quote: Wampas were typically solitary hunters.
dimorphism_note: Legends image: female and cubs (one sex shown).
note: Canon: "occasionally hunted in packs". Captive/"trained" wampas exist but no domestication. Captive wampas only; no domestication statement.

subject: Mudhorn
social_quote: The mudhorn was an extremely territorial creature by nature
domestic_quote: By 3626 BBY, mudhorns had been domesticated and used as riding animals and pet companions.
note: "hard to domesticate them; only expert handlers were able to do it". Domestication evidence is Legends (SWTOR mount).

subject: Strill
social_quote: Strills were territorial creatures, marking the areas they claimed as their own
domestic_quote: a number of Mandalorians took to keeping strills

subject: Bogwing
social_quote: It was very territorial and used its talons to pick up victims.
note: Juveniles flock under successful hunters for scraps.

subject: Gizka
domestic_quote: All the attempts at domesticating the gizka ended in disaster
note: Fast-breeding colony pest ("a temporary colony of gizka").

subject: Dalgo
domestic_quote: Onderon rebels used dalgos as beasts of burden and battle mounts

subject: Igitz
domestic_quote: The igitz were a popular pet in most Gungan civilizations.

subject: Puffer pig
domestic_quote: Puffer pigs were raised as livestock for consumption by residents of the planet Batuu.

subject: Convor
social_quote: in the jungles of Wasskah they worked in pairs to fend off predators
domestic_quote: Convorees were popular as pets throughout the galaxy.

subject: Bolotaur
domestic_quote: Bolotaurs were sometimes tamed and used as mounts.

subject: Gelagrub
domestic_quote: They were easily domesticated creatures whose larval forms were used as mounts

subject: Worrt
domestic_quote: Worrts could, with great difficulty, be trained as housepets.

subject: Saw-toothed grank
domestic_quote: imported saw-toothed granks were sold as pets or zoo animals

subject: Jamel
domestic_quote: Jamels were used as beasts of burden by the Utapau Amani.

subject: Orray
domestic_quote: Many orrays were tamed and domesticated by the Geonosians

subject: Runyip
domestic_quote: were still commonly used a pack animals on frontier worlds

subject: Tee-muss
domestic_quote: Tee-muss were a species of domesticated farm animals

subject: Gorg
domestic_quote: sewers, where harvesters bred them illegally; and gorgmonger farms
note: Longtail/Frilled gorg are donor-mod subspecies with no Wookieepedia page of their own - NOT sourced as canon; inherit gorg only if the owner says so.

subject: Blarth
domestic_quote: Amiable and easily tamed, they were kept as a household pet and watch animal by Gungans

subject: Can-cell
domestic_quote: The Wookiees of Kashyyyk considered the appearance of a can-cell a good omen, and often kept them as pets.

subject: Dactillion
domestic_quote: They were also used as mounts in battle by the Utapaun Security Forces

subject: Lava flea
domestic_quote: The creatures were easily domesticated

subject: Blurrg
domestic_quote: two-legged reptilian beast of burden found throughout the galaxy
dimorphism_note: Males eaten by females after mating (behaviour, not look).
note: Only "herd" is a Legends game store price ("a herd of 12").

subject: Nuna
domestic_quote: made them popular livestock animals
dimorphism_note: the male nunas could inflate when agitated (large anterior body cavity).

subject: Yobshrimp
domestic_quote: fishing families cultivated the foreign yobshrimp for consumption

subject: Boma
domestic_quote: one Mandalorian clan existing that has bred the vicious bomas for centuries in their breeding pens
note: Legends; bred as war beasts.

subject: Loth-cat
social_quote: Loth-cats led solitary lives, coming together only to mate and raise kits.
domestic_quote: Although it was very difficult, loth-cats could be domesticated
note: Social contradictory: another reference says family groups.

subject: Acklay
domestic_quote: also took to breeding them
note: Captive-bred arena beasts, not tame.

subject: Krayt dragon
note: Canon and Legends pages silent on grouping; lone-individual stories only. Sanity probe did NOT return SOLITARY.

subject: Dragonsnake
dimorphism_note: King of the Dragonsnakes "a large individual male" (one individual).

subject: Sarlacc
dimorphism_note: Females generally grew much larger than males; male attaches to female like an anglerfish (Legends).
note: Our def is an invented mobile form. Jabba's "pet" is one captive.

subject: Sando aqua monster
dimorphism_note: canon_references/sandoaquamonster legends_1 shows male and female (female has belly pores); text: males over 200 m, females at least 150 m.
note: Elder/Storm Sando are our invented morphs.

subject: Opee sea killer
dimorphism_note: Male mouth-broods eggs (behaviour).
note: Crimson Opee is our invented morph.

subject: Colo claw fish
note: Abyssal/Thornback are our invented morphs.

subject: Laa
note: Only an image caption "A group of laas".

subject: Dianoga
dimorphism_note: Hermaphroditic; gender is self-identified, not a body difference.
note: "A family of dianoga inhabited a pool" (one anecdote).

subject: Urusai
dimorphism_note: Females had two wings, while males had four (Legends; images show females only).
note: Nests in sarlacc maws.

subject: Wraid
social_quote: Wraids were often seen in clusters from two to six members.
note: WraidAlpha is our invention.

subject: Shiro
note: "very popular with Gungan cooks" - eaten, not kept.

subject: Granite slug
note: Deliberately introduced to Coruscant to eat garbage.

subject: Hssiss
social_quote: When in the lakes on Ambria, they hunted in pairs
note: One pet (Ktriss, Great Bogga's).

subject: Blixus
note: One pet (D'Nar's).

subject: Ollopom
note: One pet in a tank (Dok-Ondar).

subject: Qormot
social_quote: rival qormots or predators encroached on the territory of their small prides
note: Small territorial prides; also wiki category "Herd and pack creatures".

subject: Skalder
domestic_quote: They were not normally ridden by sentient beings

subject: Great Devourer
note: One named individual.

subject: Ysalamiri
social_quote: Many ysalamiri grouped together would expand their Force-neutral bubble
note: "large groups of ysalamiri could extend their collective bubble"; one pet shown at a livestock exchange.

subject: Brain worm
note: Parasite; herd/pack not applicable.
